rows.answer: The environmental objectives are: climate change mitigation; climate change adaptation; the sustainable use and protection of water and marine resources; the transition to a circular economy; pollution prevention and control; and the protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems [4].

The minimum safeguards must ensure alignment with the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, including the principles and rights in the eight fundamental ILO conventions and the International Bill of Human Rights [1]. Passage [2] describes the same requirement.

An economic activity is considered to significantly harm climate change mitigation where it leads to significant greenhouse gas emissions, taking into account the life cycle of its products and services [1].

Under the CSRD, sustainability reporting must cover the impacts of the undertaking's activities on people and the environment, and how sustainability matters affect the undertaking. These two perspectives together form the double materiality approach [3].
Large public-interest entities that are large undertakings with more than 500 employees must report for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2024 [4].
The Commission must adopt assurance standards for reasonable assurance of sustainability reporting by means of delegated acts no later than 1 October 2028 [1][3].

The management report must be prepared in the electronic reporting format specified in Article 3 of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/815, with sustainability reporting marked up in accordance with that format once it is determined [1][2]. The sustainability statement must also be presented in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable [3].
The medium-term time horizon runs from the end of the short-term reporting period up to 5 years [3].

Irrespective of the outcome of its materiality assessment, the undertaking must always disclose the ESRS 2 General Disclosures (all Disclosure Requirements and data points in ESRS 2) and the Disclosure Requirements (including their datapoints) in topical ESRS related to Disclosure Requirement IRO-1 [3][1].

Disclosure Requirement E1-6 – Gross Scopes 1, 2, 3 and Total GHG emissions asks the undertaking to disclose its gross Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 GHG emissions, plus total GHG emissions, in metric tonnes of CO2eq [2][3][4].

An economic activity qualifies as contributing substantially to an environmental objective as an enabling activity when it directly enables other activities to make a substantial contribution to one or more of those objectives, provided it (a) does not lead to a lock-in of assets that undermine long-term environmental goals, considering the economic lifetime of those assets, and (b) has a substantial positive environmental impact on a life-cycle basis [1].

Non-financial undertakings must disclose the proportion of their turnover, the proportion of their capital expenditure, and the proportion of their operating expenditure associated with environmentally sustainable economic activities [1][5].

Third-country undertakings that generate a net turnover of more than EUR 150 million in the Union and have a subsidiary undertaking or a branch in the Union are subject to Union sustainability reporting requirements [1]. For a branch, the branch itself must have generated more than EUR 40 million in net turnover in the preceding financial year, and the EUR 150 million group-level test still applies [1][2][3].

The CSRD first requires a **limited assurance** engagement, starting with an obligation on the statutory auditor or audit firm to express an opinion on the sustainability reporting's compliance with Union requirements [1]. The passages do not say that the CSRD is a "limited assurance" regime in its full, long-term form, so I'm answering only for the initial stage described in [1].
The Commission had to adopt the first set of sustainability reporting standards by 30 June 2023. [1][5]

The Commission must review the sustainability reporting standards every three years to take account of relevant developments [1]. Passages [2] and [3] likewise require review at least every three years after the date of application.
EFRAG (the European Financial Reporting Advisory Group) provides the Commission with technical advice on sustainability reporting standards [2][3][5].

The long-term time horizon is more than 5 years, as defined in paragraph 77(c) of ESRS 1 section 6.4 [3]. Paragraph 79 notes that other ESRS may define different time horizons for specific disclosures, and those definitions prevail [1].

Disclosure Requirement E1-1 – Transition plan for climate change mitigation covers this, as the passage states that "The undertaking shall disclose its transition plan for climate change mitigation" [2]. The table of contents and the Appendix A application requirements also list it under the Strategy heading [1][4].
The GWP values used to calculate CO2-equivalent emissions of non-CO2 gases must be the most recent IPCC values based on a 100-year time horizon [1].
